questions.question: Your agent's JSON output sometimes refunds more than the order total. Validation alone would reject it. What's better?
options: Crash and alert a human every time
Send the violation back to the model as a precise message and let it retry, with a bounded retry count
Accept it and fix it later
Lower the temperature
questions.explanation: Errors are observations. A clear message plus a retry limit usually gets a valid answer on the next call.

questions.question: How does a Pydantic AI agent deliver a structured output?
options: It prints JSON in a text reply
The model calls a final_result tool whose arguments are validated against the output type
It writes to a file
Through a system prompt
questions.explanation: Output is a tool call, so the same validate-and-retry machinery handles tools and output.

questions.question: Why do tools take a RunContext instead of reading a global database client?
options: It's faster
Dependencies are injected per run, so tests can pass fakes and production can pass real clients
Globals are not allowed in Python
The model needs to see the database
questions.explanation: ctx.deps carries services into tools without globals, and ctx isn't part of the schema the model sees.

questions.question: The model replies with plain text, but output_type is RefundDecision. What happens?
options: The text is returned
It gets a retry message asking it to answer with a tool call
The run ends with None
The text is parsed with regex
questions.explanation: Plain text isn't a valid typed answer, so it counts as an output retry.

questions.question: With the default retries=1, the model returns an invalid final_result twice in a row. What happens?
options: It retries forever
UnexpectedModelBehavior is raised after the retry limit is exceeded
The invalid output is returned
The agent switches models
questions.explanation: One retry is allowed; a second failure exceeds the limit and raises.

questions.question: Why should validation report all field errors at once?
options: It looks nicer
The model can fix every problem in one retry instead of spending one call per field
Pydantic requires it
It reduces token usage of the system prompt
questions.explanation: Each retry is a model call. One complete error message saves calls and retries.
